We've sent a clear message: these criminal activities are no longer tolerated, and cartels are not welcome here. Our commitment to securing our communities and protecting those along the border remains unwavering.

VOICE victim liaisons:
 
—Help victims and their family members understand the immigration enforcement and removal process
—Provide access to social service professionals to refer victims to resources and service providers
—Help victims and their family members receive automated custody status information on criminal aliens

Toll free hotline: 855-48-VOICE, Monday-Friday 8 A.M. to 8 P.M. ET.

Celebrating the one-year anniversary of the Trump Administration's VOICE Office relaunch.

items.description: An excerpt of VP JD Vance's White House press-briefing remarks on Iran ('Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon'), with a red headline card, burned-in captions, and a 'TEXT VP TO 45470' lower-third. items.description: Video. A 2018 DHS 'If You See Something, Say Something' counterterrorism PSA showing travelers at a hotel valet, a restaurant, and a family at an outdoor party, with a voiceover asking people to stay aware of their surroundings and report suspicious activity to local authorities. It is a narrated awareness spot with no music track. It predates the second Trump administration. | Travel is part of the American way of life. Everyone plays a role in keeping our community safe. Whether you're traveling for business or pleasure, be aware of your surroundings. If you see something suspicious, say something to local authorities. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.description: Video. Acting DHS Secretary Chad Wolf delivers a direct-to-camera address in a studio (US flag, CISA seal on screen) outlining CISA's COVID-19 critical-infrastructure and cybersecurity work, with brief B-roll of a call-center worker. It is an institutional informational message driven by continuous speech, not a music track. | to the dedicated professionals of DHS. As you know, this department is utilizing each component to combat the COVID-19 outbreak. Today, I'd like to talk to you about the unique efforts that the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has contributed to our shared mission. Under the leadership of Director Chris Krebs, CISIS serves as a nation's risk advisor coordinating with our interagency, state, local, and private sector partners to spread awareness of the pandemic's impact on our critical infrastructure. One of CISIS's most important contributions has been its guidance on the essential critical infrastructure workforce. This guidance is a valuable resource for state and local partners as they make decisions regarding essential services and how to keep them up and running during stay at home orders. items.description: Video. DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas speaks direct-to-camera against a blue curtain, with a lower-third name plate and burned-in subtitles, describing DHS's anti-human-trafficking work for Human Trafficking Prevention Month. It is a static informational message driven entirely by speech, with no music track and no fast cutting. | Hello, I am Alejandro Mayorkas, Secretary of the United States Department of Homeland Security. The Department of Homeland Security has a critical role in the fight against human trafficking. This work touches nearly every part of our department. Our extraordinary special agents identify, save, and protect victims, and they investigate and arrest the traffickers. We deliver support to survivors of human trafficking to ensure their safety and stability. We provide immigration relief to non-citizen trafficking victims and their families. We ensure that goods produced by forced labor do not come into our country. We train law enforcement on how to recognize indicators of human trafficking. And we raise public awareness about this horrific crime through the DHS Blue Campaign. This is truly a DHS-wide mission. Our department's belief in the dignity of the in

items.description: Video. Cardell Morant, Director of the DHS Center for Countering Human Trafficking, speaks direct-to-camera against a blue curtain with a lower-third name plate and subtitles, describing the Center's anti-trafficking work. It is a static, speech-driven institutional informational message with no music. | When most people first learn about human trafficking, they are shocked and frankly overwhelmed by the sheer scale of the problem and the fact that this is happening here in the United States and around the world. Given the seriousness of this crime, there is always an urgency to this work, whether it's in prevention, prosecution, or protection. With this in mind, DHS came together and not only developed a department-wide counter-trafficking strategy which we are guided by today, but also launched the DHS Center for countering human trafficking in 2020. Every day, I am incredibly proud to lead the team that meets this center's vital mission, the center oversees the department's work to combat human trafficking and the importation of goods produced with forced labor. Learn more about the Blue Campaign from Program Manager, Brandi B.⬇️ https://t.co/nciFLmgI79
items.description: Video. Brandi Bynum, Program Manager of the DHS Blue Campaign, speaks direct-to-camera against a blue curtain with a name plate and subtitles, intercut with informational text-card slides listing the Blue Campaign's long-term outcomes. It is a speech-driven awareness explainer with no music and no fast cutting. | Blue Campaign is a national public awareness campaign designed to educate the public, law enforcement, community partners, and frontline employees on how to recognize and respond to suspected human trafficking. Blue Campaign also works closely with DHS component agencies to develop general awareness trainings, as well as specific educational resources to help reduce victimization within vulnerable populations. We are also home to the Blue Lightning Initiative, which is led by the Department of Transportation and US Customs and Border Protection. The Blue Lightning Initiative partners with airlines and others in the aviation industry to train staff on how to recognize and report suspected human trafficking they may observe on the job. It is an educational explainer driven by narration, not a music track. | Throughout our nation's airports, approximately 48,000 transportation security officers remain vigilant day in and day out to protect the traveling public from threats crossing our security checkpoints. These threats come in many different forms, one of those being human trafficking. Human trafficking infringes people's human rights, exploits them for labor and sex, and robs them of their liberty. TSA trains all transportation security officers to report and recognize indicators of human trafficking, which may be exhibited by both the victim and the trafficker. Transportation security officers are trained to look out for indicators of potential victims including signs of physical and emotional abuse, bruises in various stages of healing, behaviors indicating the person was coached to speak and or act in a certain manner, or fearful, timid, or submissive behavior. items.description: A holiday cyber-safety video in which a CISA spokesperson wearing a Christmas sweater speaks to camera in front of a CISA step-and-repeat backdrop, advising viewers to use multi-factor authentication, shop trusted sources, and avoid phishing, ending at cisa.gov/shopsafely. Sissa wants everyone to enjoy the holiday season, but we know that while you're breaking out your ugly sweater, bad actors are trying to steal your joy, your identity, and your money. How can you stop these scrooches in their tracks? First, always ensure you have multi-factor authentication turned on. Passwords can be hacked, so add one more level of security, your fingerprint, your face, something only you have. Second, shop through trusted sources, and watch out for fishing emails. Never give your account info out via text for email. Finally, if your password is still 12345, you're getting a hole in your stock. Learn more at sissa.gov slash shop safely. Happy Holidays! | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.description: An audiogram from the DHS Blue Campaign '#TacklingTrafficking' series: a static blue graphic with a play icon and audio-waveform animation plays a recorded clip of Forensic Interview Specialist Lauren G. saying that trafficking victims are typically groomed rather than kidnapped, with her words shown as text-card captions. There is no video footage and no music, only narrated interview audio over a fixed graphic. | Unlike what is portrayed in the media, trafficking victims are groomed by the trafficker and not necessarily randomly kidnapped. It is not out of the realm of possibility, however, and there have been known cases of individuals being kidnapped because they began to uncover the trafficker's scheme and decide they no longer wanted to be a part of it, so they are taken by force and held against their will. But that typically happens after the victim has been in the situation for some time. So this is another myth which has been around for many years as it was the thing to look for when kidnappings first started making way into the lives of so many families here in the United States. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tag

items.description: Video. A Know2Protect PSA on online child sexual exploitation built from talking-head interviews with ICE special agents (Steven Moran, Ben Miller) plus title graphics and a closing URL card. It consists of interview testimony, with no music track. | The threat of child online exploitation has never been bigger. In the 20 years I've been working, I've never seen this many leads come in. We see that taking different forms, but essentially it's when an adult offender is targeting a juvenile in the online or digital environment with the ultimate goal of some sort of sexual victimization. People don't know that this crime is happening at such an alarming rate because it is uncomfortable to talk about. Bringing it to the forefront can help prevent the crime from happening in the first place. One of the things that we always want parents to understand is predators go where the kids are. In the past playgrounds, parks, public places, that's where offenders would go. Now, the digital environment is the playground for these kids. The Notaprotect campaign will educate and empower children, teens, parents, trusted adults and policymakers to prevent and combat online child sexual exploitation

📞855-48-VOICE   

💻http://ICE.gov/voice https://t.co/KvQtknZQLL
items.description: Footage of ICE Director Todd Lyons speaking at a podium during the VOICE office reopening event, thanking victims' families by name and describing the public safety mission, with families standing behind him. It is a captioned speech clip with no music track. On-screen text reads 'TODD LYONS ICE DIRECTOR', 'TOLL-FREE VOICE HOTLINE: 855-48-VOICE (855-488-6423)', and 'VICTIMS OF IMMIGRATION CRIME ENGAGEMENT 1-855-48-VOICE'. | I know it's not easy to do, but your courage is beyond amazing. It helps us on our Dominic, Alexis, Kayla, Matthew, Weston, Nick, Ronald, and Drew, as we pursue justice for other families that have been told apart by crimes of the immigration nexus. Your stories give us a small glimpse into the struggles you face every day, and the battles you fight just to find some type of measure for the justice for your children. This also helps people understand how important the ICE public safety mission is. To make the voice office keep evolving, to provide better resources and better support to others who have lost so much at the hands of criminal aliens. And thank you again for sharing your children's stories today.

A group of DC-based journalists, the White House Correspondents' Association, has long dictated which journalists get to ask questions of the President of the United States.

Not anymore.

Today, I was proud to announce that we are giving the power back to the people.

Moving forward, the ‘White House Press Pool,’ will be determined by the White House Press Team. 

Legacy outlets who have participated in the press pool for decades will still be allowed to join – but we will also be offering the privilege to well-deserving outlets who have never been allowed to share in this awesome responsibility.

—Promoting prostitution of a child under 18, 1st degree felony: 20 years
—Compelling prostitution of a child under 18, 1st degree felony: 20 years
—Sexual performance of a child under 14, 1st degree felony: 99 years
—Possession of CSAM/video, 2nd degree felony: 20 years
—Possession of child CSAM/video, 1st degree felony: 75 years and a $5,000 fine

items.tweet_text:
.@POTUS: "From 1776 to 2026, America has always stood as a great and moral cause. Our warriors are no mere mercenaries, they are guardian angels who stride across the battlefields of history and stand watch over the highest and most beautiful planes the human spirit has ever seen—holding the line between liberty and tyranny, between civilization and barbarism, between good and evil. Wherever the American Soldier walks, wherever he fights... and wherever he falls, he does it for the destiny of a nation like no other... and for the fate of Freedom on this earth...

By their deaths, those who have gone before us in battle have redeemed the promise of our Founding for each future generation.

They've not just made the Ultimate Sacrifice, they have offered the Ultimate Proof that we Americans do indeed love Liberty. We do cherish the self-government given to us by our forefathers. We do believe with all our souls in the mission that God has given to America. And we do intend with all our strength and heart to hold high the torch our heroes handed to us—and we will never, ever let it fall."

items.tweet_text:
.@POTUS: "Scripture tells us, 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful servants.' 400,000 souls rest on these grounds... in this sacred soil, which was first consecrated in the hour of America’s greatest Division to be an eternal symbol of our National Unity. It cannot be by chance alone that the very first servicemember laid to rest here, in this place of supreme sacrifice, was a Union Soldier by the name of Private Christman—Private William Henry Christman of Pennsylvania, who died at 19 years old...

Beside him are more than 18,000 other young men named William, over 20,000 named John, over 13,000 named James, joined over time by Issacs, Elijahs, Earls, Hanks, Helens... and others whose names tell the true story of American Greatness...

LATEST CONSPIRATOR SENTENCED IN 13-YEAR ICE HSI ILLICIT SOFTWARE PROBE

A Florida woman got 22 months in prison and a $50,000 fine March 2 for trafficking illicit certificate of authenticity labels that bear Microsoft software activation codes.

Heidi Richards was sentenced in a 13-year, nationwide ICE @HSIKansasCity-led probe into a trafficking network that collectively harvested and resold at a discount over 600,000 illicit key codes worth over $900 million.

The labels and codes made counterfeit software appear legitimate.

The investigation so far includes $20.6 million in seized assets, as well as arrests, indictments and convictions of nine major distributors. DOJ calls this the largest software prosecution in its history.

A ready @USCG starts with a healthy workforce.

Through Force Design 2028, we’re forging a more agile, capable, and responsive maritime fighting force. To accelerate that effort, the Service is launching the Physical Readiness Program, to include mandated daily physical training and body composition compliance.

Nutrition is a key element. Senior Chief Sonata Haley shares practical nutrition tips that support energy, focus, and resilience, because readiness begins with taking care of our people.

Proper nutrition means you won’t just be fit for duty, you’ll be fit for life.

On National Medal of Honor Day, we honor the legacy of our sole recipient, Signalman 1st Class Douglas Munro.

On September 27, 1942, he made the ultimate sacrifice at Guadalcanal, using his boat to shield 500 Marines from enemy fire. Douglas Munro’s selfless actions and unwavering commitment to his shipmates continue to inspire every member of the #USCG to this day. His heroism, for which he posthumously received the Medal of Honor, exemplified the Coast Guard’s sacred trust with the American people and our bond with our fellow armed services.

@DHSgov 

#SemperParatus

How did #USCG Cutter Polar Star celebrate its 50th birthday? By breaking a cruise ship free from Antarctic ice.

This was just one moment in the successful 55-day Operation Deep Freeze. The Polar Star’s crew also carved a 7-mile channel, enabling the delivery of millions of gallons of fuel and a new pier for the U.S. Antarctic Program. As the United States' only heavy polar icebreaker, the Polar Star's performance underscores its indispensable role in maintaining strategic year-round access to the polar regions. This is global impact – facilitating commerce and defending America’s national interests in these critical and challenging environments.

After 14,000 miles, the crew is heading home. Bravo Zulu on a historic deployment!

The Key Bridge collapse underscored the significance of America’s Marine Transportation System, our vital network of ports and waterways. As efforts continue toward rebuilding the Key Bridge, the Coast Guard is steadfast in our resolve to respond to contingencies and facilitate commerce vital to economic prosperity.

@DHSgov @CBP @USBPChiefRGV @USBPChiefTCA

POLICE WEEK: FAMILY WELCOME
 
Over the past several days, the families of our fallen heroes have gathered in Washington, D.C., to honor the lives, service, and sacrifice of their loved ones during National Police Week.
 
We welcome them with gratitude and respect, and remind them that they do not walk this path alone. We see your strength, share in your pride, and remain humbled by your resilience.
 
While the nation honors these heroes, we recognize the enduring loss carried by their families. Your sacrifice will never be forgotten.

POLICE WEEK: VALOR MEMORIAL & WREATH LAYING 🕊️
 
Today, the U.S. Border Patrol honored the men and women who gave their lives in service to our nation during the CBP Valor Memorial and Wreath Laying Ceremony.
 
This year, two additional names were solemnly added to the Valor Memorial — forever joining the ranks of those who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.
 
Their courage, service, and devotion to protecting the American people will never be forgotten. We honor their memory, stand beside their families, and carry forward their legacy each day we wear the badge.

Always ready for the call, on and off the pitch.
 
From protecting waterfront stadiums to interdicting illicit activity, the Coast Guard is layering maritime security for FIFA World Cup 2026. Alongside our partner agencies, we’re deploying specialized capabilities to secure ports and waterways, counter threats, and respond to contingencies.

A criminal illegal alien from Mexico, has been arrested in relation to Saturday’s shooting targeting Border Patrol agents in Chicago. The suspect has a previously been convicted for aggravated unlawful use of a weapon/vehicle, felony possession of a weapon, and illegal entry.

He is currently marked as a violator of the Laken Riley Act, pending charges related to assaulting officers. 
 
This incident is not isolated and reflects a growing and dangerous trend of violence and obstruction. items.description: A local TV news segment ('DIGGING DEEPER / FRAUD IN MINNESOTA / TARGETED REVIEW') with an anchor reporting on a Department of Labor review of alleged unemployment-insurance fraud in Minnesota, including a full-screen quote card from Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer. It is a news broadcast. | Digging deeper tonight into being termed a targeted review of potential fraud in Minnesota's unemployment insurance program. It's the latest federal probe into allegations of financial wrongdoing this one by the U.S. Department of Labor. The Secretary of Labor, writing in a letter sent to the Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development, quote, I am appalled at what we are hearing about potential fraud coming from numerous benefits programs in Minnesota. If there has been any related abuse of our U.I. systems, it will not be tolerated. End quote. U.I., by the way, is a reference to unemployment insurance. The Labor Secretary says the Department's Chicago Regional Office has started a review of its benefit payment control operations to ensure no fraud is identified in unemployment insurance programs, including those during the COVID-19 pandemic.

On January 21, ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) responded to a request from the Sherburne County Sheriff’s Office in Zimmerman, MN, to help locate a missing 7-year-old girl after an AMBER Alert. HSI teams braved sub-freezing temperatures, canvassed neighborhoods, and worked closely with local law enforcement, gathering surveillance information to aid the search.
 
On January 22, HSI was notified that the child was found safe and the alleged sexual assaulter and kidnapper, 28-year-old Joseph Andrew Bragg, was taken into custody.
 
HSI is proud to have helped bring this young girl home and ensure alleged child predators are removed from Minnesota’s streets.

items.tweet_text:
Our ICE officers and agents are HEROES.

On March 25, 2026, an ICE agent helping to support @TSA operations at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York jumped into action to help save the life of a one-year-old child experiencing a medical emergency.

The heroic actions of this officer began when a one-year-old child became unresponsive in the arms of his father, unable to breathe for almost two minutes. CCTV review shows a passenger in a TSA Precheck line holding his one-year-old in his arms when the child’s arms go lifeless; panic ensues, and the father is seen scrambling around the area, and calling for help.  

The agent working at his post, heard the screams from the father and other passengers and sprinted to the scene. The father handed the child to the officer, who then assessed the unresponsive child and began performing the Heimlich maneuver. After a few seconds, the child started breathing again. EMS personnel arrived on scene with medical equipment to further monitor and re-assess the child. The child was re-assessed and determined to be healthy enough to fly.

Johnathan Brown, 34, secretly recorded young girls, hiding outside bedroom windows and placing cameras inside a laundry basket to record minors after they exited showers.

Special thanks to the Butler Township Police Department, Miami Valley Human Trafficking Task Force and @OSHP.

I wouldn't want to do it, but it takes people like this to make our country great. And again, I've never seen anything. Everybody I knew they went to see the launch, and they especially wanted to see a successful landing. And Jared, I want to congratulate you, what you've done at NASA. I made a great choice. Las Vegas police arrested John Young Cotter Johnstone, an illegal alien from the UK, who police say was captured on video dragging and swinging dogs by their leashes and kicking one dog.

Johnstone faces multiple charges connected to animal abuse he allegedly committed while working at a local rescue in Nevada.

The same day Johnstone was arrested, ICE issued an immigration detainer with the Clark County Detention Center. The next day, April 2, Clark County officials honored the detainer, and ICE took custody of the alleged animal abuser.

Johnstone came to the United States under the Visa Waiver Program as a visitor. He was supposed to leave the country by Feb. 22, 2022. 

ICE secured a final order of removal. He’ll stay in ICE detention pending local charges.

items.description: NBC News Now sit-down interview of Secretary Rubio (US flag behind, NBC logo) discussing the Straits of Hormuz and a UN resolution on Iran. Static interview shot with reporter, continuous talking, no music. | Did President Trump raise the issue of Iran with China? He did, and it was important because the Chinese side said they are not in favor of militarizing the Straits of Hormuz, and they're not in favor of a tolling system. And that's our position. We will never support an Iranian tolling system in the Straits of Hormuz, nor do we think they have a right to put minds in international waters. And so it's good that we have alliance, or at least agreement on that point. I think the fundamental question is what are we going to do about it? We have a resolution now before the United Nations, in which 100 and something countries have co-signed. The Bahrainis are the sponsor, but we're strongly behind it, and we've been pushing very hard on it. And it very clearly makes those points. So we hope the Chinese will vote for it. So right now we haven't gotten their commitment to vote for it yet at the United Nations. Maybe that'll change after today's meeting. I don't know. | Reviewed video

"We're continuing to ramp up U.S. natural gas exports," says @SecretaryWright in Louisiana.

"It will be a record again this year. It was a record last year. We're up to about 20 Bcf/day of natural gas that we export, which is roughly double the 2nd and 3rd largest exporters." https://t.co/XkHum2y72s
items.description: Vertical video. Energy Secretary Wright speaks in Louisiana about record US natural gas exports and LNG capacity. A talking-head interview, with no music or added production. | Yeah, we're continuing to ramp up U.S. natural gas exports. It'll be a record again this year, it was a record last year. We're up to about 20 BCF a day of natural gas that we export, which is roughly double the second and third largest exporters of natural gas, cutter being one of those two countries. So it is tough to have lost that 10 BCF a day of gas exports right now, but we're adding about two and a half BCF a day of export capacity in the United States just this year. So a quarter that'll be filled by growth from U.S. exports today. Now of course demand is growing too. Price mechanism right now is going to reduce the growth of LNG this year, but that's a temporary interruption. Traffic will be flowing through the Straits of Hormuz as soon as we can, but certainly sometime this summer it later. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

items.description: FTC's Ferguson in a seated interview describing AI fraud-detection systems used by the White House Fraud Task Force. And what we were able to do basically, sort of like building on the doge effort, is work with these agencies with the data that they have, the data that other agencies have, and publicly available data, and build technological solutions, most of which are AI-driven that can take all of these data. And so when a claims payment request comes in, basically AI puts up a flag and says, very likely fraudulent. And all of the agencies have administrative authority to withhold those payments until they know that this is a real person that's actually qualifying for this request. If you have to do that by hand, if you have to have individuals go out and figure all these out, the money just goes out the door, and then you have to get the doge to chase it and they can't get it all back. So using these advanced automated technological solutions, that's the way you supercharge the effort

🚨AMO Black Hawk disabling fire ends vessel pursuit🚨

On May 13, AMO aircrews detected a suspicious 25-foot Yola-type vessel northwest of Puerto Rico, carrying three individuals and visible packages. Our teams maintained continuous aerial surveillance, tracking the vessel through the night.

The next evening, the San Juan Marine Unit launched a coordinated interdiction operation. Two Coastal Interceptor Vessels and multiple aircraft moved in, guided by constant vectors from our aircrews.

At 9:51 p.m., the targeted vessel was intercepted north of San Juan. The suspects tried to evade capture and began dumping contraband into the water. In a decisive moment, the AMO Black Hawk crew deployed Air Disabling Fire, stopping the vessel cold.

Three Dominican Republic nationals were taken into custody, and five bales containing 391 lbs. of cocaine were seized and transferred to the Homeland Security Task Force. This operation highlights our relentless commitment to securing America’s borders and keeping dangerous drugs off our streets. 

Check out the full video here: https://ow.ly/TVYb50Z5kFS#SecuringAmerica 

#AMO #BorderSecurity #Teamwork

items.description: Video. A TV 'Exit Interview' clip of Secretary Mayorkas (talking head with a subtitle bar) discussing drone sightings over New Jersey and asking Congress to expand DHS authorities. It is a broadcast interview, with no music. | And let me restate what we've said previously. It's very important. We know of no threat to people's security. And if we learn of any cause for concern, we will take action and we will communicate immediately with the American public. There are, and there have been thousands and thousands of drones flown across the United States for years. All drones, recreational drones, law enforcement drones. I spoke with an expert yesterday who has recorded over his home in California over the past six years, more than 13,000 drone detections. And so this is actually not a new phenomenon. What we need in the federal government is we need our authorities to catch up with the development of drone activity over the last 10 years. And so we have asked Congress for not only an extension of our authorities, but an expansion of them. | Reviewed video keyframe (direct frame analysis); media form recorded via the candidate tags above.

DETAINER ISSUED FOR ALLEGED NC MURDERER

Venezuelan national Angelvis Jesus Quintero Fernandez was arrested for allegedly shooting a man to death in Mecklenburg County, NC, Jan. 24.

ICE issued a detainer on him with the Mecklenburg County Jail March 23 to prevent him from reentering the community.
items.description: Horizontal video. A local TV news package about a Venezuelan national charged in a Mecklenburg County, NC murder. It includes a stand-up reporter, the suspect's mugshot, and on-screen fact bullets. It is a broadcast news clip reposted by ICE, with no music track. | We just learned Fernandez is being held without bond and has a court-appointed public defender. Fernandez is facing first-degree murder charges and it is related to the deadly shooting of 44-year-old Ludvin Guzman Morales along Central Avenue on January 24. Court records show that Fernandez was arrested yesterday and investigators say a break in the case came just days ago when officers responded to an attempted murder on Albumor Road. During the investigation, police say they found a gun inside Fernandez's car. They say he later admitted to shooting the victim after examining that weapon detectives believe it may be linked to the shooting of Guzman Morales. Now Fernandez also has an ice detainer meaning he could be taken into federal custody here at the Mecklenburg County Court House Fernandez is expected to be seen again on April 14th.

EXCLUSIVE VIDEO: Disabling fire needed to stop non-compliant vessel with 64 Illegal Aliens onboard!
 
On May 9, our Michel O. Maceda Marine Unit detected and interdicted a non-compliant Yola-type vessel carrying 64 individuals on the western side of Puerto Rico.
 
Marine Interdiction Agents discovered 64 illegal aliens from the Dominican Republic and Haiti onboard. The subjects were transferred onto AMO and PRPD FURA marine assets and transported to the Mayaguez Port of Entry. Border Patrol agents, with support from HSI and PRPD, processed the group at the Ramey Border Patrol Station for removal proceedings. #BorderSecurity
